hints: Look carefully at the two starter tubes. Pure DNA with 14N sits high up near the top, pure DNA with 15N sits low down near the bottom, so where would DNA of in-between density sit?
Remember what happens in one round of semi-conservative replication when a double 15N helix is copied using only 14N nucleotides. What will each new DNA molecule contain?
walkthrough:
**Read the centrifuge positions**

Think of the tube like a density scale. Light DNA floats high, heavy DNA sinks low.

From the diagram, $^{14}$N-$^{14}$N DNA = top band, $^{15}$N-$^{15}$N DNA = bottom band.

**Apply semi-conservative replication for one generation**

The starting bacteria have both strands heavy ($^{15}$N). They are moved to light ($^{14}$N) medium and divide once.

Each parental strand separates and acts as a template, and each new strand is built from light $^{14}$N. So every new molecule is hybrid:
$$1 \text{ old } ^{15}\text{N strand } + 1 \text{ new } ^{14}\text{N strand}$$

**Predict the band**

All the DNA after one division is identical hybrid DNA. Its density is exactly halfway between light and heavy.

So we expect one single band in the middle of the tube, and that matches tube D perfectly.

options.A: Shows two bands, one intermediate and one heavy. After one division there is no pure heavy DNA left, so this is incorrect.
options.B: Shows a single light band at the top. That would need two fully light strands, which cannot form after only one division starting from heavy DNA.
options.C: Shows one light and one heavy band. That is the prediction of conservative replication, not the semi-conservative replication that actually occurs.
options.D: Shows one single intermediate band. This is exactly right because all DNA molecules are $^{15}$N-$^{14}$N hybrids after one round of semi-conservative replication.
